issues.description: The problem statement (UML and method list) specifies checkOrderReady() as returning void, but the provided solution implements checkOrderReady() with a boolean return type. This discrepancy can confuse students about the correct method signature to implement and may cause mismatches with tests or the intended API.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the method signature across artifacts. Either change the solution's checkOrderReady() to return void (removing the boolean return value and any returned expressions) to match the UML/specification, or update the problem statement and tests to document and require a boolean return type. Preferably keep the signature void as described in the problem statement so students implement checkOrderReady(): void.
